title: Reject the measured ingestion-adaptive shuffle pilot
question: Does same-buffer ingestion admission followed by fitting Fisher-Yates avoid enough complete-job cost?
summary: Remove the single-buffer adaptive prototype after no demonstrated complete-job benefit; preserve lossless-transition source/tests/evidence without additional tuning.

workloads: 12000 by 192-byte fitting and 50000 by 192-byte external root-auto cells; three alternating pairs each.

validation.summary: Actual fitting FY selection and external three-run/one-merge path verified; source IDs/fields/order conservation, parser-relief/threshold transition and cancellation controls passed before removal.

limitations: Overlapping elapsed ranges and mixed paired signs do not establish consistent slowdown.
No WASI or native Windows performance experiment; no restored resident-data selector.
Small warm WSL2/bundled-Chromium development samples do not establish native Windows/macOS, other browsers, scale or tails.
Working reservations are not RSS; Analysis temporary counters precede publication; final committed-head CI is separate.
An inherited parser-owned shrink replacement-overlap gap remains in unchanged baseline producers; new mixed-prefix intake retains actual capacity.
Private archive readback used the existing OAuth principal; no separate scoped-reader or public publication claim.
exclusions: Warmups, failed attempts and source-mismatched/quarantined WASM output are excluded from measured comparisons.
Derived summaries and repeated verification records are not additional observations; cells/runtimes are not pooled.
reopen_when: Reopen only for a concrete ingestion-integrated cost reduction that changes complete-job economics without a second complete spool or raw reread.
